prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for everyone — the right one depends on your situation (income, health needs, whether you want Marketplace/ACA plans or off‑exchange plans, interest in HSAs, willingness to pay broker fees, etc.). I can help you pick one, but first here are practical ways to find the best broker in Kansas City for a self‑employed person and some reputable options to consider.

What to look for in a broker for the self‑employed
- Experience with ACA/Marketplace plans and subsidy eligibility (important if you qualify for premium tax credits).  
- Familiarity with solo/self‑employed issues (quarterly estimated taxes, HSA‑eligible plans, high‑deductible plans).  
- Independent (able to show plans from multiple carriers) vs. captive (works for one insurer). Independent is usually better for comparison shopping.  
- Transparent about fees/commissions — many consumer‑facing brokers are paid by carriers, but some charge a fee for extra help.  
- Good reviews and credentials (state license, NAHU membership, Google/Yelp ratings).  
- Willingness to enroll you, answer post‑enrollment questions, and help with claims or plan changes.

Places and brokers to consider
- HealthSherpa — strong for Marketplace/ACA plans, straightforward subsidy handling, enrollment support.  
- eHealthInsurance — large comparison site for on‑ and off‑exchange plans; good for comparing carrier options.  
- Policygenius — user‑friendly search and quotes, good for comparing options.  
- Stride (or similar gig‑worker services) — tailored tools for independent contractors and gig workers in some areas.  
- Local independent insurance agencies in Kansas City — many local agencies can help compare Blue KC, UnitedHealthcare, Ambetter, Cigna, Humana, etc. (look for “independent” in their descriptions).

How to find reputable local brokers
- Use the NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) “Find an Agent” tool.  
- Search Google/Yelp for “health insurance broker Kansas City” and read recent reviews.  
- Check the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup to confirm the agent is licensed.  
- Ask other self‑employed people or local small‑business groups/Chamber of Commerce for referrals.  
- Community “Certified Navigators” or assisters can help with ACA enrollment at no cost during open enrollment.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- Do you work with Marketplace (ACA) plans and can you help determine subsidy eligibility?  
- Are you independent or tied to a single carrier? Which carriers do you represent?  
- Do you charge clients a fee for your services? If so, how much and when is it due?  
- What post‑enrollment support do you provide (claims help, plan changes, renewals)?  
- Can you show side‑by‑side comparisons including premiums, deductibles, OOP max, network, and drug coverage?

Next step
If you want, tell me your ZIP code, whether you expect to qualify for premium tax credits (approximate income), and whether you prefer Marketplace plans or private/off‑exchange plans. I can look up highly rated local brokers or give more specific recommendations based on your needs.
